title: Sketch aids

courses.title: Lesson 0 · Where the sketch aids are
courses.objective: Find all nine sketch aids: in the ribbon before you sketch, and in the SKETCH AIDS bar inside a sketch.
courses.challenge: Turn two aids on at once, then turn both off again.

steps.title: Start a sketch on the Front plane
steps.learn: Aakar draws a sketch on a flat plane. The Front plane is the one that faces you, like the front of the block.
instructions: Press Do it for me, or press Sketch (K) and choose the Front plane.
steps.why: Snapshot and the other aids work inside a sketch, so we open one first.

checkpoint.expected: The sketch editor is open and the SKETCH AIDS bar is along the top of the drawing.

steps.recovery: Not open? Press Sketch in the ribbon, then click the Front (orange) plane.

guide.now: Start a sketch on the Front plane.

steps.title: Find the SKETCH AIDS bar
steps.learn: Look along the top of the drawing. A row of round buttons is there: Guides, Snapshot, Helix, Onion skin, Clearance, Live 3D, Wall thickness, Slices, Trace picture. An orange button means that aid is on.
instructions: Look at the top of the drawing area.
Hover over a button. A tip explains what it does.
steps.why: One click turns an aid on or off. You never have to dig through menus.

checkpoint.expected: You can see the bar of buttons.

steps.recovery: Bar missing? You are not inside a sketch. Press Sketch (K).

guide.now: Look at the top of the drawing. Press Got it when you can see the bar.
guide.cap: The SKETCH AIDS bar sits above the drawing.

steps.title: Switch one aid on
steps.learn: Click Onion skin. The button turns orange. Click it again and it turns off.
instructions: Press Do it for me, or click Onion skin in the bar.
steps.why: Aids are safe: they only show extra help on screen. They never change your model.

checkpoint.expected: The Onion skin button is orange.

steps.recovery: Not orange? Click the Onion skin button once.

guide.now: Click Onion skin in the bar.

steps.title: Open the settings
steps.learn: The last button, Settings, opens a long panel. Each aid has a line of explanation, and some have a number you can change.
instructions: Click ⚙ Settings at the end of the bar.
Read the list. Click Settings again to close it.
steps.why: Numbers such as the clearance in mm live here.

checkpoint.expected: The Sketch aids panel is open on the left.

steps.recovery: Nothing opened? Click the dashed ⚙ Settings button.

guide.now: Click ⚙ Settings, read the list, then press Got it.
guide.cap: Settings lists every aid with its numbers.

steps.title: Start from the ribbon
steps.learn: Before you sketch, the ribbon has a Sketch aids button in the Model tab. Pick an aid from its menu. Aakar opens a sketch for you (on the selected face, or you choose a plane) and switches that aid on.
instructions: Finish this sketch (press Finish).
In the Model tab, press Sketch aids and look at the menu.
steps.why: You do not have to remember the order: ribbon first, or sketch first.

checkpoint.expected: You know both ways in.

steps.recovery: Cannot find the button? It is in the Model tab, between Check & export and Convert.

guide.now: Look at the Sketch aids button in the Model tab, then press Got it.
nums: a sketch with the aid on

steps.title: What you learned
steps.learn: The aids live in the ribbon and in the bar above every sketch.
instructions: Read the summary, then press Got it.
steps.why: A short recap helps the idea stick.

checkpoint.expected: You can say what the aid does and when to use it.

steps.recovery: Want to see it again? Press Start again.

guide.now: Press Got it to finish.
guide.cap: Done. The aids live in the ribbon and in the bar above every sketch.

courses.title: Lesson 1 · Snapshot: the whole model as reference lines
courses.objective: Freeze the model, seen along your sketch plane, as lines you can snap to and measure from. Then try the cross-section.
courses.challenge: Take a snapshot from behind (Look from: From behind) and compare.

steps.title: Make the practice block
steps.learn: You need a part with a hole. This lesson uses a block 60 by 40 mm and 20 mm tall, with a round blind hole 16 mm across. The hole is not in the middle: it sits 28 mm back from the front.
instructions: Press Do it for me. Aakar draws the block and cuts the hole.
Or build your own: a 60 by 40 rectangle extruded 20 mm, then a 16 mm circle on top cut 12 mm deep.
steps.why: A hole that is off to one side is the usual case. It shows why the sketch aids matter.

checkpoint.expected: A block with a round hole in the top face appears in the 3D view.

steps.recovery: Nothing appeared? Press Do it for me again. Already have a part with a hole? Use it and skip this step.

guide.now: Press “Do it for me” to make the block with the hole.

steps.title: Start a sketch on the Front plane
steps.learn: Aakar draws a sketch on a flat plane. The Front plane is the one that faces you, like the front of the block.
instructions: Press Do it for me, or press Sketch (K) and choose the Front plane.
steps.why: Snapshot and the other aids work inside a sketch, so we open one first.

checkpoint.expected: The sketch editor is open and the SKETCH AIDS bar is along the top of the drawing.

steps.recovery: Not open? Press Sketch in the ribbon, then click the Front (orange) plane.

guide.now: Start a sketch on the Front plane.

steps.title: Open the Snapshot menu
steps.learn: Press Snapshot in the bar. A menu opens with choices: what to capture, how (outline or cross-section), which side, how detailed, and replace or add.
instructions: Click Snapshot in the SKETCH AIDS bar.
Read the choices. Do not take it yet.
steps.why: You decide how the snapshot is made, so it always shows what you need.

checkpoint.expected: The Snapshot menu is open.

steps.recovery: Menu not there? Click the Snapshot button in the bar (camera icon).

guide.now: Click Snapshot in the bar, read the menu, then press Got it.

steps.title: Take an outline snapshot
steps.learn: Outline captures what you would see looking at the plane: the silhouette and the visible edges. The lines are light blue and you can snap to them.
instructions: Press Do it for me, or choose Outline and press Take snapshot.
steps.why: The block's edges are now real reference lines: snap to them, or measure from them.

checkpoint.expected: Light blue lines in the shape of the block's front appear.

steps.recovery: No lines? Check that Solids is ticked, then press Take snapshot.

guide.now: Choose Outline and press Take snapshot.

steps.title: Show the hidden edges
steps.learn: Tick Also show hidden edges and take it again. Hidden edges are dotted, like looking through the block.
instructions: Press Do it for me, or tick Also show hidden edges and press Take snapshot.
steps.why: Dotted lines show what is behind the front face, such as the floor of the hole.

checkpoint.expected: Some dotted lines appear.

steps.recovery: Nothing dotted? Make sure the choice is Outline and that Also show hidden edges is ticked.

guide.now: Tick “Also show hidden edges”, then press Take snapshot.

steps.title: Try the cross-section
steps.learn: Cross-section cuts the model with the sketch plane and shows the cut outline in bright white. Set the cut offset to -28 to cut right through the hole.
instructions: Press Do it for me, or choose Cross-section, type -28 for the offset and press Take snapshot.
steps.why: A cross-section shows the inside: hole walls, floor and thickness.

checkpoint.expected: A bright outline of the block with the hole cut out appears.

steps.recovery: Nothing? The cut may miss the part. Try -28 mm here.

guide.now: Choose Cross-section, set the offset to -28, press Take snapshot.
guide.cap: The cut shows the hole inside the block.

steps.title: Remove the snapshot
steps.learn: Press Remove in the Snapshot menu to clear it. The lines go away; your own sketch is untouched.
instructions: Press Remove in the menu.
steps.why: A snapshot is only a helper. You can take a new one any time.

checkpoint.expected: The reference lines are gone.

steps.recovery: Still there? Open Snapshot and press Remove.

guide.now: Press Remove in the Snapshot menu, then press Got it.

steps.title: What you learned
steps.learn: Snapshot makes reference lines from the model. You choose outline or cross-section.
instructions: Read the summary, then press Got it.
steps.why: A short recap helps the idea stick.

checkpoint.expected: You can say what the aid does and when to use it.

steps.recovery: Want to see it again? Press Start again.

guide.now: Press Got it to finish.
guide.cap: Done. Snapshot makes reference lines from the model. You choose outline or cross-section.

courses.title: Lesson 2 · Draw a thread tooth inside a hole
courses.objective: Your hole sits behind the Front plane, so the plane misses it. Move the sketch plane through the hole's axis and draw the thread tooth right inside the circle.
courses.challenge: Do the same from the Side plane instead.

steps.title: Make the practice block
steps.learn: You need a part with a hole. This lesson uses a block 60 by 40 mm and 20 mm tall, with a round blind hole 16 mm across. The hole is not in the middle: it sits 28 mm back from the front.
instructions: Press Do it for me. Aakar draws the block and cuts the hole.
Or build your own: a 60 by 40 rectangle extruded 20 mm, then a 16 mm circle on top cut 12 mm deep.
steps.why: A hole that is off to one side is the usual case. It shows why the sketch aids matter.

checkpoint.expected: A block with a round hole in the top face appears in the 3D view.

steps.recovery: Nothing appeared? Press Do it for me again. Already have a part with a hole? Use it and skip this step.

guide.now: Press “Do it for me” to make the block with the hole.

steps.title: Start a sketch on the Front plane
steps.learn: Aakar draws a sketch on a flat plane. The Front plane is the one that faces you, like the front of the block.
instructions: Press Do it for me, or press Sketch (K) and choose the Front plane.
steps.why: Snapshot and the other aids work inside a sketch, so we open one first.

checkpoint.expected: The sketch editor is open and the SKETCH AIDS bar is along the top of the drawing.

steps.recovery: Not open? Press Sketch in the ribbon, then click the Front (orange) plane.

guide.now: Start a sketch on the Front plane.

steps.title: See that the plane misses the hole
steps.learn: Take an outline snapshot. The block shows, but the hole barely shows: this plane is 28 mm in front of the hole.
instructions: Press Do it for me. Then look at the Snapshot menu list: “Round holes & shafts”.
steps.why: To draw a thread inside a hole you need a plane that cuts through it.

checkpoint.expected: The menu says the plane misses the hole by 28 mm.

steps.recovery: No list? Open Snapshot and look under Round holes & shafts.

guide.now: Take an outline snapshot and read the hole list.

steps.title: Move the plane through the hole axis
steps.learn: Press “Sketch plane through axis: Front (XZ)” under the hole. Aakar moves the sketch plane to the hole's centre and keeps what you drew.
instructions: Press Do it for me, or press the button under the hole in the Snapshot menu.
steps.why: Now the plane slices through the hole, so you see its walls and floor.

checkpoint.expected: The status line says “XZ plane @ 28 mm” and the hole's walls and floor are shown.

steps.recovery: Nothing moved? Open Snapshot and press Sketch plane through axis.

guide.now: Press “Sketch plane through axis” under the hole.
guide.cap: The plane now cuts through the hole.

steps.title: Draw the tooth inside the circle
steps.learn: The hole wall on the left is a vertical line. Draw the tooth as a small four-sided shape that sticks out from that wall into the hole.
instructions: Press Do it for me, or draw four lines: (22, 12), (23.1, 12.45), (23.1, 12.75), (22, 13.2). Close the shape.
steps.why: This small shape is one turn of the thread. A sweep will repeat it round a helix later.

checkpoint.expected: A closed tooth shape touches the left wall of the hole.

steps.recovery: Shape not closed? Draw the last line back to the first point.

guide.now: Draw the closed tooth shape on the hole wall.
guide.cap: The tooth sits on the hole wall.

steps.title: Add the red helix guide
steps.learn: Press Helix in the bar. Red dashed lines appear one pitch apart (1.5 mm). They show where each next turn of the thread will sit.
instructions: Press Do it for me, or click Helix and type 1.5 for the pitch.
steps.why: The red lines help you check the tooth and the spacing before you make the thread.

checkpoint.expected: Four red dashed lines start from the lowest point of the tooth.

steps.recovery: Not visible? Click Helix again; the first click asks for the pitch.

guide.now: Click Helix and use 1.5 mm for the pitch.

steps.title: Finish the sketch
steps.learn: Press Finish. The tooth is saved as a sketch you can sweep along a helix.
instructions: Press Do it for me, or press Finish.
steps.why: Finished sketches show in the Features list and can be used by other tools.

checkpoint.expected: The sketch appears in the Features list.

steps.recovery: Still sketching? Press the green Finish button.

guide.now: Press Finish.

steps.title: What you learned
steps.learn: A hole off the plane is found for you, and one button moves the plane through its axis.
instructions: Read the summary, then press Got it.
steps.why: A short recap helps the idea stick.

checkpoint.expected: You can say what the aid does and when to use it.

steps.recovery: Want to see it again? Press Start again.

guide.now: Press Got it to finish.
guide.cap: Done. A hole off the plane is found for you, and one button moves the plane through its axis.

courses.title: Lesson 3 · Smart guides
courses.objective: Let pink guides line your drawing up with the model: corners, centres, midpoints and equal gaps.
courses.challenge: Draw a line that lines up with two different corners.

steps.title: Make the practice block
steps.learn: You need a part with a hole. This lesson uses a block 60 by 40 mm and 20 mm tall, with a round blind hole 16 mm across. The hole is not in the middle: it sits 28 mm back from the front.
instructions: Press Do it for me. Aakar draws the block and cuts the hole.
Or build your own: a 60 by 40 rectangle extruded 20 mm, then a 16 mm circle on top cut 12 mm deep.
steps.why: A hole that is off to one side is the usual case. It shows why the sketch aids matter.

checkpoint.expected: A block with a round hole in the top face appears in the 3D view.

steps.recovery: Nothing appeared? Press Do it for me again. Already have a part with a hole? Use it and skip this step.

guide.now: Press “Do it for me” to make the block with the hole.

steps.title: Start a sketch on the Front plane
steps.learn: Aakar draws a sketch on a flat plane. The Front plane is the one that faces you, like the front of the block.
instructions: Press Do it for me, or press Sketch (K) and choose the Front plane.
steps.why: Snapshot and the other aids work inside a sketch, so we open one first.

checkpoint.expected: The sketch editor is open and the SKETCH AIDS bar is along the top of the drawing.

steps.recovery: Not open? Press Sketch in the ribbon, then click the Front (orange) plane.

guide.now: Start a sketch on the Front plane.

steps.title: Give the sketch something to line up with
steps.learn: Guides line up with points that already exist. Take a cross-section snapshot so the block's outline is there to use.
instructions: Press Do it for me, or take a cross-section snapshot (offset -28).
steps.why: Guides need references. A snapshot supplies them from the model.

checkpoint.expected: A bright outline of the cut block is in the sketch.

steps.recovery: No outline? Open Snapshot, choose Cross-section, offset -28, Take snapshot.

guide.now: Take a cross-section snapshot (offset -28).

steps.title: Switch Smart guides on
steps.learn: Click Guides in the bar. It turns orange.
instructions: Press Do it for me, or click Guides.
steps.why: Guides only appear when you use a draw tool, so they never get in the way.

checkpoint.expected: The Guides button is orange.

steps.recovery: Not orange? Click Guides once.

guide.now: Click Guides in the bar.

steps.title: Pick the Line tool
steps.learn: Press Line in the sketch toolbar (or press L). Guides need a draw tool to be active.
instructions: Click the Line tool, then move the pointer over the drawing.
steps.why: While a draw tool is active, the pointer looks for points to line up with.

checkpoint.expected: The Line tool is active.

steps.recovery: Press L on the keyboard if you cannot find the button.

guide.now: Pick the Line tool, then press Got it.

steps.title: Watch the pink guides
steps.learn: Move the pointer slowly near a corner of the outline. A pink dashed line appears, with a note such as “aligned with face corner”. The pointer snaps onto it.
instructions: Move the pointer near a corner, then to the same height as another corner.
Click to start a line where a pink guide shows.
steps.why: You can place points exactly in line with the model without typing any numbers.

checkpoint.expected: You saw a pink dashed guide and a note beside the pointer.

steps.recovery: No guide? Move closer (within a few pixels), and make sure a draw tool is on.

guide.now: Move near corners and watch for pink guides, then press Got it.

steps.title: Find the middle
steps.learn: Move the pointer to the middle between two vertical lines. The guide says “same gap” and shows the distance on both sides.
instructions: Move between two parallel lines until “same gap” shows.
steps.why: Centring a feature between two edges is one of the most common jobs.

checkpoint.expected: You saw “same gap” with a distance on each side.

steps.recovery: Try moving slowly across the middle of the block.

guide.now: Find the middle between two lines, then press Got it.

steps.title: What you learned
steps.learn: Smart guides line you up with corners, centres, midpoints and equal gaps.
instructions: Read the summary, then press Got it.
steps.why: A short recap helps the idea stick.

checkpoint.expected: You can say what the aid does and when to use it.

steps.recovery: Want to see it again? Press Start again.

guide.now: Press Got it to finish.
nums: a draw tool and reference lines
guide.cap: Done. Smart guides line you up with corners, centres, midpoints and equal gaps.

courses.title: Lesson 4 · Helix guide
courses.objective: See where each next turn of a thread tooth will sit, before you make the thread.
courses.challenge: Change the pitch to 2 mm and see the red lines move apart.

steps.title: Start a sketch on the Front plane
steps.learn: Open a sketch on the Front plane.
instructions: Press Do it for me, or press Sketch (K) and choose the Front plane.
steps.why: The helix guide needs a profile to measure from.

checkpoint.expected: The sketch editor is open.

steps.recovery: Press Sketch in the ribbon and click Front.

guide.now: Start a sketch on the Front plane.

steps.title: Draw one tooth
steps.learn: Draw a small four-sided shape: a tooth of a thread. It is 1.1 mm tall and 0.75 mm wide.
instructions: Press Do it for me, or draw (10, 2), (11.1, 2.45), (11.1, 2.75), (10, 3.2) and close it.
steps.why: The guide starts from the lowest point of whatever you draw.

checkpoint.expected: A closed tooth shape is in the sketch.

steps.recovery: Not closed? Draw the last line back to the first point.

guide.now: Draw the closed tooth shape.

steps.title: Switch the helix guide on
steps.learn: Click Helix in the bar and type the pitch, 1.5 mm. Red dashed lines appear, one pitch apart.
instructions: Press Do it for me, or click Helix and enter 1.5.
steps.why: Pitch is the distance the thread moves forward in one full turn. The lines show it.

checkpoint.expected: Four red dashed lines, each labelled with its height.

steps.recovery: Click Helix again if the first click only asked for the pitch.

guide.now: Click Helix and use 1.5 mm.

steps.title: Read the lines
steps.learn: The first line says “start of turn 1”. The next say “turn 2 · +1.5 mm”, “turn 3 · +3 mm”. The next tooth will start on the next line.
instructions: Look at the red lines and their labels.
steps.why: A thread is the same tooth repeated at each line. If your tooth does not fit between lines, the pitch is wrong.

checkpoint.expected: You can say where turn 2 starts.

steps.recovery: Zoom in (mouse wheel) if the labels are small.

guide.now: Read the red labels, then press Got it.

steps.title: What you learned
steps.learn: The red guide shows one pitch per turn.
instructions: Read the summary, then press Got it.
steps.why: A short recap helps the idea stick.

checkpoint.expected: You can say what the aid does and when to use it.

steps.recovery: Want to see it again? Press Start again.

guide.now: Press Got it to finish.
guide.cap: Done. The red guide shows one pitch per turn.

courses.title: Lesson 5 · Onion skin
courses.objective: See your old sketch as a faint ghost while you edit, so you can see what your change moves.
courses.challenge: Move the circle back to where the ghost is.

steps.title: Make a disc
steps.learn: A circle sketch, extruded 8 mm. We will edit its sketch next.
instructions: Press Do it for me.
steps.why: You need something saved to edit.

checkpoint.expected: A round disc appears.

steps.recovery: Press Do it for me again.

guide.now: Press “Do it for me” to make the disc.

steps.title: Edit its sketch
steps.learn: Double-click Disc sketch in the Features list. The sketch opens again.
instructions: Press Do it for me, or double-click Disc sketch in the Features list.
steps.why: Onion skin remembers how the sketch looked the moment you opened it.

checkpoint.expected: You are back in the sketch editor.

steps.recovery: Double-click the first item in the Features list.

guide.now: Double-click Disc sketch in the Features list.

steps.title: Switch Onion skin on
steps.learn: Click Onion skin in the bar.
instructions: Press Do it for me, or click Onion skin.
steps.why: From now on a faint orange copy stays where the sketch started.

checkpoint.expected: The button is orange.

steps.recovery: Click Onion skin once.

guide.now: Click Onion skin in the bar.

steps.title: Move the circle
steps.learn: Drag the circle to the right. An orange ghost stays behind at the old place.
instructions: Press Do it for me, or select the circle and drag its centre.
steps.why: You can see the old and new together, so you know what changed.

checkpoint.expected: An orange circle (old) and a blue circle (new) are side by side.

steps.recovery: Select the centre point and drag it.

guide.now: Drag the circle to the right.

steps.title: What you learned
steps.learn: Onion skin keeps a ghost of the sketch as it was when you opened it.
instructions: Read the summary, then press Got it.
steps.why: A short recap helps the idea stick.

checkpoint.expected: You can say what the aid does and when to use it.

steps.recovery: Want to see it again? Press Start again.

guide.now: Press Got it to finish.
guide.cap: Done. Onion skin keeps a ghost of the sketch as it was when you opened it.

steps.title: Move the plane through the hole

steps.title: Switch Clearance bands on
steps.learn: Click Clearance in the bar. A teal band appears round the reference lines.

checkpoint.expected: A teal band runs along the hole walls.

steps.recovery: Click Clearance once.

guide.now: Click Clearance in the bar.

steps.learn: Draw a small shape 0.3 mm from the left wall. Each point close to the wall gets a label: “fit 0.3 mm”, “too tight 0.1 mm”, or “gap …”.
instructions: Press Do it for me, or draw four points around x = 22.3 and 23.5.

instructions: Open ⚙ Settings.

checkpoint.expected: The band gets thinner or wider.

steps.recovery: Press Enter after typing the number.

guide.now: Change the clearance number, then press Got it.

steps.learn: Clearance bands show the tolerance zone and tell you fit or too tight.
instructions: Read the summary, then press Got it.

checkpoint.expected: You can say what the aid does and when to use it.

steps.recovery: Want to see it again? Press Start again.

guide.now: Press Got it to finish.

courses.title: Lesson 7 · Live 3D preview
courses.objective: See the profile you draw as a solid: extrude, revolve and thread, in a small window you can turn.
courses.challenge: Make the tooth taller and watch the thread change.

steps.title: Start a sketch on the Front plane
steps.learn: Open a sketch on the Front plane.
instructions: Press Do it for me, or press Sketch (K) and choose the Front plane.
steps.why: The preview shows the profile you draw.

checkpoint.expected: The sketch editor is open.

steps.recovery: Press Sketch in the ribbon and click Front.

guide.now: Start a sketch on the Front plane.

steps.title: Draw a closed shape
steps.learn: Draw the tooth: four lines that close.
instructions: Press Do it for me, or draw (10, 2), (11.1, 2.45), (11.1, 2.75), (10, 3.2) and close it.
steps.why: The preview needs a closed profile.

checkpoint.expected: A closed tooth shape is in the sketch.

steps.recovery: Close the shape with a last line.

guide.now: Draw the closed tooth shape.

steps.title: Switch Live 3D on
steps.learn: Click Live 3D in the bar. A small window appears with your shape as an extrusion. Drag in it to turn it.
instructions: Press Do it for me, or click Live 3D.
steps.why: You see the solid before you finish the sketch.

checkpoint.expected: A window shows a blue 3D shape.

steps.recovery: Click Live 3D once.

guide.now: Click Live 3D in the bar.

steps.title: Try Revolve
steps.learn: Press Revolve in the little window. The shape spins round the vertical axis: a ring.
instructions: Press Do it for me, or press Revolve in the 3D window.
steps.why: Revolve is how bottles, cups and wheels are made.

checkpoint.expected: The window shows a ring.

steps.recovery: Press the Revolve button in the 3D window.

guide.now: Press Revolve in the 3D window.

steps.title: Try Thread
steps.learn: Press Thread. The tooth is swept round and up: a real helical thread, 3 turns at 1.5 mm pitch.
instructions: Press Do it for me, or press Thread in the 3D window.
steps.why: This is exactly what a thread feature will build.

checkpoint.expected: The window shows a spiral.

steps.recovery: Press the Thread button in the 3D window.

guide.now: Press Thread in the 3D window.

steps.title: What you learned
steps.learn: Live 3D shows your profile as extrude, revolve or thread while you draw.
instructions: Read the summary, then press Got it.
steps.why: A short recap helps the idea stick.

checkpoint.expected: You can say what the aid does and when to use it.

steps.recovery: Want to see it again? Press Start again.

guide.now: Press Got it to finish.
guide.cap: Done. Live 3D shows your profile as extrude, revolve or thread while you draw.

courses.title: Lesson 8 · Wall thickness
courses.objective: Tint the cut outline by how thick the material is, and find the thinnest wall.
courses.challenge: Set the minimum wall to 5 mm. Which parts turn red?

steps.title: Make the practice block
steps.learn: You need a part with a hole. This lesson uses a block 60 by 40 mm and 20 mm tall, with a round blind hole 16 mm across. The hole is not in the middle: it sits 28 mm back from the front.
instructions: Press Do it for me. Aakar draws the block and cuts the hole.
Or build your own: a 60 by 40 rectangle extruded 20 mm, then a 16 mm circle on top cut 12 mm deep.
steps.why: A hole that is off to one side is the usual case. It shows why the sketch aids matter.

checkpoint.expected: A block with a round hole in the top face appears in the 3D view.

steps.recovery: Nothing appeared? Press Do it for me again. Already have a part with a hole? Use it and skip this step.

guide.now: Press “Do it for me” to make the block with the hole.

steps.title: Start a sketch on the Front plane
steps.learn: Aakar draws a sketch on a flat plane. The Front plane is the one that faces you, like the front of the block.
instructions: Press Do it for me, or press Sketch (K) and choose the Front plane.
steps.why: Snapshot and the other aids work inside a sketch, so we open one first.

checkpoint.expected: The sketch editor is open and the SKETCH AIDS bar is along the top of the drawing.

steps.recovery: Not open? Press Sketch in the ribbon, then click the Front (orange) plane.

guide.now: Start a sketch on the Front plane.

steps.title: Cut through the hole
steps.learn: The wall strip measures the cut of the sketch plane. Move the plane through the hole.
instructions: Press Do it for me.
steps.why: Through the hole you can see the floor and walls.

checkpoint.expected: The sketch plane is at 28 mm.

steps.recovery: Open Snapshot and use Sketch plane through axis.

guide.now: Move the sketch plane through the hole axis.

steps.title: Switch Wall thickness on
steps.learn: Click Wall thickness in the bar. This lesson uses a minimum wall of 10 mm so you can see red.
instructions: Press Do it for me, or click Wall thickness.
steps.why: Red means thinner than your minimum. Green means comfortable.

checkpoint.expected: Coloured strips run along the cut outline, and a label says “thinnest wall 8 mm”.

steps.recovery: Click Wall thickness once.

guide.now: Click Wall thickness in the bar.

steps.title: Find the thinnest spot
steps.learn: A white circle marks the thinnest place: the floor under the hole is 8 mm thick.
instructions: Look for the white circle and its label.
steps.why: Thin walls break, warp or fail in printing.

checkpoint.expected: You can say where the thinnest wall is.

steps.recovery: Zoom out if the label is off screen.

guide.now: Find the white circle, then press Got it.

steps.title: Change your minimum
steps.learn: Open ⚙ Settings and change Wall thickness “mm min” to 5. The floor turns green.
instructions: Open ⚙ Settings, change the number, press Enter.
steps.why: Your own rule: 1.5 mm for plastic, 3 mm for metal, and so on.

checkpoint.expected: The colours change.

steps.recovery: Press Enter after typing.

guide.now: Change the minimum wall, then press Got it.

steps.title: What you learned
steps.learn: Wall thickness colours the cut and marks the thinnest spot.
instructions: Read the summary, then press Got it.
steps.why: A short recap helps the idea stick.

checkpoint.expected: You can say what the aid does and when to use it.

steps.recovery: Want to see it again? Press Start again.

guide.now: Press Got it to finish.
guide.cap: Done. Wall thickness colours the cut and marks the thinnest spot.

courses.title: Lesson 9 · Layer slices
courses.objective: Show faded cuts of the model in front of and behind your sketch plane.
courses.challenge: Change the step to 4 mm. How many cuts reach the hole?

steps.title: Make the practice block

instructions: Press Do it for me. Aakar draws the block and cuts the hole.
Or build your own: a 60 by 40 rectangle extruded 20 mm, then a 16 mm circle on top cut 12 mm deep.

steps.recovery: Nothing appeared? Press Do it for me again. Already have a part with a hole? Use it and skip this step.

guide.now: Press “Do it for me” to make the block with the hole.

steps.title: Start a sketch on the Front plane
steps.learn: Aakar draws a sketch on a flat plane. The Front plane is the one that faces you, like the front of the block.
instructions: Press Do it for me, or press Sketch (K) and choose the Front plane.

steps.title: Switch Slices on
steps.learn: Click Slices in the bar. Faded outlines appear: blue ones in front, pink ones behind, each labelled with its distance.
instructions: Press Do it for me, or click Slices.
steps.why: You see the shape of the part at several depths without leaving the sketch.

checkpoint.expected: Faded blue and pink outlines with labels like +7 mm and -14 mm.

steps.recovery: Click Slices once.

guide.now: Click Slices in the bar.

steps.title: Find the hole
steps.learn: One of the slices cuts through the hole: its outline has a notch. That slice is 28 mm away.
instructions: Look for the outline with the notch.
steps.why: This tells you where the hole is, in depth, without changing planes.

checkpoint.expected: You found the slice with the hole.

steps.recovery: Zoom out to see all the slices.

guide.now: Find the slice with the notch, then press Got it.
guide.cap: The slice at 28 mm shows the hole.

courses.title: Lesson 10 · Trace a picture
courses.objective: Turn a reference picture into lines you can snap to and measure from.
courses.challenge: Trace the picture, then draw a circle that snaps onto the outline.

steps.title: Add a picture
steps.learn: A sample bottle picture is added on the Front plane. You can add your own with Tools › Reference images.
instructions: Press Do it for me.
steps.why: Tracing needs a picture placed on the sketch plane.

checkpoint.expected: A picture of a bottle appears in the view.

steps.recovery: Press Do it for me again, or import a picture with Tools › Reference images.

guide.now: Press “Do it for me” to add the sample picture.

steps.title: Start a sketch on the Front plane
steps.learn: Open a sketch on the Front plane. The picture shows behind your drawing.
instructions: Press Do it for me, or press Sketch (K) and choose Front.
steps.why: The picture must be on the same plane as the sketch.

checkpoint.expected: The picture is behind the sketch grid.

steps.recovery: Press Sketch in the ribbon and click Front.

guide.now: Start a sketch on the Front plane.

steps.title: Trace it
steps.learn: Click Trace picture in the bar. Aakar finds the dark outline and turns it into amber lines.
instructions: Press Do it for me, or click Trace picture.
steps.why: Now the picture's outline is real geometry you can use.

checkpoint.expected: Amber lines follow the outline of the bottle.

steps.recovery: Click Trace picture once. The picture needs good contrast.

guide.now: Click Trace picture in the bar.

steps.title: Snap to the traced lines
steps.learn: Pick a draw tool and click near the amber outline. The pointer snaps to it, and you can measure from it with Smart dimension.
instructions: Pick the Line tool and click on the amber outline.
steps.why: Trace first, then draw your clean version on top.

checkpoint.expected: Your line starts exactly on the amber outline.

steps.recovery: Move closer to the amber line.

guide.now: Draw a line that starts on the amber outline, then press Got it.

steps.title: Remove the traced lines
steps.learn: Click Trace picture again to remove the amber lines.
instructions: Click Trace picture again.
steps.why: Your own geometry stays.

checkpoint.expected: The amber lines are gone.

steps.recovery: Click Trace picture once more.

guide.now: Click Trace picture again, then press Got it.

instructions: Read the summary, then press Got it.
